transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Recorded by: Fireflies

[00:00] Jordan Patel (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Maya Rivera (Arcadia): Maya here, hello.
[00:07] Ethan Cole (Arcadia CTO): Ethan on from engineering.
[00:09] Priya Nair (Finance): Priya here.
[00:11] Liam O'Sullivan (Compliance): Liam in the call.
[00:12] Jordan Patel: Great. Sofia, want to take the perf recap?
[00:17] Sofia Kim (Redwood SE): Yeah, quick summary — we ran the tuned model with the latency-optimized profile and the small KV cache change; P95 latency is ~85ms on the host config we used, P99 around 210ms during the 10k concurrent run. Average token cost after batching and prefix cache reductions sits around $0.0028 per 1k tokens in our sample workload, caveat that the numbers vary by prompt length.
[00:44] Ethan Cole: Okay, 85ms P95 sounds good — was that with the dedup cache on? I remember there's a toggle on the prefix caching.
[00:50] Sofia Kim: Yes, we enabled prefix caching for the common templates and ran two runs: one with cache warm and one cold. Cold run P95 spiked to ~140ms, warm run sits in the 70–90ms window.
[01:10] Maya Rivera: And accuracy? We care about hallucinations in the triage flow — we had a previous note of a 6% hallucination rate in the seeded evals.
[01:18] Sofia Kim: Right, after prompt rework and a light sampling temperature change we've dropped hallucination to ~3.5% on the test set — still some edge cases around rare drug codes, which we're marking for a follow-up prompt/validation rule.
[01:35] Priya Nair: From finance perspective, the projected monthly spend in the model-hosted scenario with our expected qps is in the ballpark of $21k–27k. Jordan, can you confirm how robust that estimate is?
[01:46] Jordan Patel: That spreadsheet I sent earlier included a few slices — this new tuned profile reduces token usage by ~12% compared to the first baseline, that delta is baked into the $21k estimate. There are assumptions on average prompt length and cache hit rate — if cache hit drops to 40% the number moves up.
[02:10] Priya Nair: We need a conservative and an optimistic line item for the CFO. Can we get a tight worst-case?
[02:14] Jordan Patel: Yep, I'll add a conservative column with 35% cache hit and 10% throughput burst.
[02:22] Liam O'Sullivan: Security question — for private deployment we discussed KMS and SSO earlier. Have you validated HSM/KMS integration? What about audit logs retention for clinicians?
[02:33] Sofia Kim: We ran the KMS flow in our staging private deployment; Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS and cloud KMS via the Private control plane. Audit logs are pushable to your SIEM, retention configurable. We do need a confirm from your infra team for the VPC peering egress rules — Ravi?
[02:50] Ravi Menon: I'm on it, I have a few small questions around NAT and routing but I can produce a topology tomorrow.
[02:56] Sofia Kim: Great — that'll help finalize the checklist.
[03:05] Ethan Cole: On the business case — timeline wise, if execs sign off in two weeks what's the expected lead-time for Dedicated capacity? We prefer reserved but also want an option to ramp.
[03:16] Jordan Patel: For dedicated capacity, once the contract is signed typical provisioning is 5–7 business days to get the reserved pool and network in place. If you need faster ramp we can start you on hosted while Dedicated is being provisioned and then cutover.
[03:31] Maya Rivera: That hybrid approach sounds workable if the cutover preserves session / key continuity — any migration complexity?
[03:36] Sofia Kim: The runtime supports model-compatibility and KV-cache migration; there is a small window where you might need to flush and repopulate caches, but we have patterns to reduce user-visible impact.
[03:48] Priya Nair: Procurement question — what contract terms do we need to be prepared for? Any minimum commitment?
[03:55] Jordan Patel: For Dedicated we typically ask for a 12-month reserved commit; we can structure a pilot-to-reserved path with credits applied to the commitment. Hosted no minimum. I'll share a draft commercial term sheet.
[04:07] Maya Rivera: Good. 
[04:09] Liam O'Sullivan: A few compliance asks — can Redwood provide a SOC2 Type II report and an exportable audit trail for activity? Also SAML IdP support?
[04:20] Jordan Patel: Yes to SOC2 and IdP/SAML; we also support SCIM provisioning and RBAC roles. We'll attach the compliance pack to the pipeline.
[04:30] Ethan Cole: On technical debt — we saw a failure mode during the earlier stress run where long sequences caused KV cache blowup and OOM. Have you got a mitigation?
[04:41] Sofia Kim: We pushed a guardrail — an eviction policy and token-length caps for the session. In the run after we applied it, memory was stable and no OOMs observed. We'll include the logs.
[04:53] Maya Rivera: Excellent. Next — can we align on final success criteria for the business case? I'll read what I think the execs will want and you tell me if Redwood can meet it.
[05:01] Maya Rivera: Success criteria draft: (1) P95 latency <= 100ms at steady-state (2) monthly cost <= $30k with our QPS profile (3) Hallucination rate <= 5% on seeded evals (4) Security signoff: SOC2 + KMS + SSO + audit logs (5) Integration completed with two pilot clinics by end of Q3.
[05:21] Priya Nair: That looks right; CFO will want the cost threshold explicit and the decision window.
[05:26] Jordan Patel: We can meet 1–4 given the current configs; for item 5 the integration timeline depends on their internal EMR connector work but Redwood can commit to supporting rollout to two pilot clinics in the given window if the clinic-side integration is staffed.
[05:42] Ethan Cole: Any remaining technical blockers from Redwood side?
[05:45] Sofia Kim: No blockers; we flagged the rare drug-code hallucination cases and will ship filtered validation rules. We also want to validate SSO flows with your staging IdP prior to exec signoff.
[05:58] Ravi Menon: I'll stand up a staging IdP tonight and share credentials with Sofia.
[06:03] Jordan Patel: Great, that'll unblock compliance checks.
[06:07] Maya Rivera: On the go/no-go runbook — can you share a short template with decision points and owners?
[06:13] Jordan Patel: Yes, we'll send a one-page runbook: decision criteria, owners, fallback plan (stay hosted vs delayed rollout), and exec meeting draft agenda.
[06:22] Priya Nair: If execs ask for a conservative spend line, can you add the 95th percentile cost scenario?
[06:28] Jordan Patel: Yep, conservative column as discussed.
[06:31] Sofia Kim: One more note — we ran a qualitative eval with clinical annotators; they reported improved triage speed and fewer false positives vs baseline, see the attached annotated spreadsheet.
[06:44] Maya Rivera: That's helpful for the business case narrative.
[06:48] Jordan Patel: OK, quick recap of owners and due dates: I'll send benchmark CSV + runbook by Friday, Sofia runs the stability pass and KMS checklist by next Monday, Maya to route runbook to execs, Priya will assemble finance slide for CFO.
[07:10] Ethan Cole: Sounds good. Anything else?
[07:12] Liam O'Sullivan: One last ask — can Redwood provide a short data-flow diagram for auditors?
[07:18] Sofia Kim: We'll attach a simplified topology diagram and a note on retention and redaction.
[07:24] Jordan Patel: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up on action items.
[07:29] Maya Rivera: Thanks all.
[07:30] End of recording.
